items.title: Strain-invariant highly conductive Janus organogels for AI-assisted bioelectronics
items.abstract: Achieving integrated conductive hydrogels with strain-invariant high conductivity and Janus adhesion for anti-interference flexible bioelectrodes remains challenging. Herein, we propose a gravity-flipping annealing strategy to realize strain-invariant (600%) organogels with ultrahigh conductivity (8 × 10⁵ S/m) and Janus adhesion (10-fold adhesion contrast) for AI-assisted bioelectronics. Rigid-flexible interlocked percolation networks formed during annealing maintain continuous conductive pathways under extreme strains, while spatially segregated aggregation of metallic liquid-solid phases generates self-organized asymmetric topographies that directly mediate Janus adhesion. Simultaneously, the organogel exhibits superior biocompatibility, tissue-like softness, self-healing, and anti-desiccation, thereby enabling stable bioelectronic performance. The engineered organogel facilitates robust bioelectrodes integrated with advanced AI architectures. These bioelectrodes enable robust electrical stimulation of sciatic nerves, quantitatively resolved via AI-powered image tracking. Moreover, the system exhibits vibration-robust monitoring of physiological signals under mechanical interference, achieved by adapting ChatGPT-inspired transformer architecture for time-series decoding. This integration of high-performance organogels with AI paves the way for next-generation bioelectronics.

items.title: From classical to AI-driven load frequency control: Addressing smart grid challenges with renewable energy sources and EVs integration
items.abstract: This research investigates advancements in Load Frequency Control (LFC) by examining AI-based and optimization-driven strategies aimed at improving frequency stability in Multi-Area Power Systems (MAPSs). The study offers a broad evaluation, transitioning from early classical approaches to emerging modern and AI-driven techniques. A key methodological contribution is the structured comparison of traditional, intelligent, and optimization-based controllers evaluated by using standardized performance indices such as ITSE under realistic system conditions, including nonlinearities (GRC, GDB, CTD) and communication delays. It assesses various control strategies, emphasizing the adaptability and robustness required for effective LFC in dynamic environments. Particular attention is also paid to optimization methods and artificial controllers. The study also evaluates the impacts of energy storage technologies, electric vehicles (EV), and renewable energy sources on the system frequency stability. Moreover, it also investigates machine learning and reinforcement learning frameworks with the potential to address LFC issues. The paper contains critical smart grid issues like potential cybersecurity threats, controller failures, data transmission errors and communication boundaries. It also introduces a systematic Scopus-based literature filtration process, resulting in a publication trend analysis that reveals evolving research directions. Providing practical insights and novel approaches, this work aims to divert future studies toward more stable, flexible, and robustness-based LFC solutions in a more practical complex power system realization.

items.title: Transformer-based renewable energy forecasting: A comprehensive review
items.abstract: Accurate renewable energy forecasting (REF) is critical for efficient power system planning, management, and operation, given the intermittent and stochastic nature of renewable energy sources (RESs). Transformer-based models have emerged as a promising solution for REF due to their superior ability to model sequential dependencies and capture complex spatiotemporal patterns. This paper presents a comprehensive and methodologically structured review of Transformer-based approaches for renewable energy forecasting, analyzing their unique advantages, inherent challenges, and practical deployment considerations. We systematically examine key Transformer variants and their applications across solar, wind, and other RESs, while establishing a generalized REF framework. A quantitative comparison with conventional deep learning techniques demonstrates that Transformer models achieve a significant improvement in forecasting accuracy. Additionally, we explore recent advancements in Transformer architectures, data preprocessing methods, and optimization strategies that further enhance their predictive performance and computational efficiency. By synthesizing current research trends, this review offers actionable insights for practitioners and identifies future directions to advance scalable and reliable Transformer-based forecasting systems. Our findings underscore the transformative potential of Transformer models in elevating the accuracy and robustness of REF, providing a valuable reference for researchers and industry stakeholders.

items.title: AI-enabled fault diagnosis for hydrogen fuel cells: recent advances, challenges, and future perspectives
items.abstract: Ensuring the operational reliability and safety of hydrogen fuel cells has become a critical research focus. The inherently coupled multi-physics nature of fuel cells gives rise to diverse and nonlinear fault mechanisms, presenting substantial challenges for conventional model-based diagnostic approaches. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a compelling alternative, owing to its strong capabilities in data-driven pattern recognition and adaptive learning. In this study, typical faults and diagnosis execution process in fuel cell systems were systematically reviewed. At the core, unlike existing reviews that primarily classify methods by algorithmic categories or application scenarios, we systematically evaluate the applicability and limitations of representative AI techniques at each diagnostic stage from data acquisition to control adaptation. Finally, the key challenges that hinder real-world deployment are discussed, and emerging research trends are prospected. This review's contribution lies in offering a new perspective by connecting diagnostic workflow requirements with AI capabilities, which reframes how researchers should match techniques to fuel cell system challenges.

items.title: Toward greener shipping: A systematic review of AI-driven solutions for environmental performance in maritime operations
items.abstract: Decarbonizing maritime transport is a central challenge for global climate policy, as the sector combines high greenhouse gas intensity with complex operational and regulatory constraints. Compliance with evolving International Maritime Organization (IMO) instruments, including the Carbon Intensity Indicator and the IMO Net-Zero Framework, requires decision-support tools capable of operating under heterogeneous data environments and operational uncertainty. In this context, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as data-driven emission-reduction strategies in maritime operations. This systematic review examines how AI/ML models are designed, validated, and applied to improve environmental performance and regulatory alignment in the maritime sector. Using a PRISMA-based methodology, peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2025 are analyzed and classified across core application domains, including predictive maintenance, performance and emissions prediction, route and speed optimization, surveillance and navigation, and design and manufacturing. The review distinguishes between base models, which emphasize predictive accuracy under controlled conditions, and robustness-oriented models, which address cross-vessel generalization, validation under variable operational scenarios, sensitivity to data uncertainty, and fleet-level transferability. The synthesis shows that while many base models achieve high predictive performance, robustness remains limited due to fragmented data standards, scarce real-world validation, and weak integration with regulatory systems. Based on these findings, three policy implications are derived: (i) standardized digital emissions and performance data formats are required to enable scalable AI deployment; (ii) AI- monitoring should be formally recognized within IMO compliance and reporting mechanisms; and (iii) regulatory incentives should prioritize robust, fleet-level AI solutions over vessel-specific pilots.

items.title: Energy harvesting in hybrid electric vehicles and railway systems: AI-enabled condition monitoring and emerging trends
items.abstract: Modern electric and hybrid transportation platforms employ numerous sensors, controllers, and communication modules that require continuous power supply. Energy harvesting technologies offer a promising solution to support these auxiliary systems and reduce dependency on the primary battery. This article systematically evaluates major energy harvesting technologies such as Thermoelectric generators (TEGs), Regenerative Braking systems (RBS), Regenerative shock absorbers (RSAs) and other vibration harvesting technologies, as the potential solution to provide the power supply in the onboard auxiliaries and self-sensing modules. A comparative analysis is presented in terms of working principles, energy conversion potential, operational characteristics, and practical implementation in transportation systems. TEGs exploit exhaust-gas thermal gradients, RBS recovers kinetic energy typically discarded as heat and RSAs transform vibrations caused by suspensions to electrical energy without affecting ride comfort. To further the discussion, the review also applies the same to railway applications where bogie, axle-box and track-mounted harvesters enabled self-powered monitoring and predictive maintenance. Adaptive power distribution, autonomous health management, and self-sustaining IoT-based transport (IoTT) further are backed up by the integration of mechanical intelligence and AI-enabled energy management. In general, this review demonstrates the prospect of multi-source hybrid harvesters to eliminate traction battery dependence and to extend the vehicle range and facilitate a fully self-powered cyber-physical transportation platform.

items.title: Material innovation and AI-driven smart packaging for fruit and vegetable precision preservation: Applications and future trends
items.abstract:
Background
Postharvest fruits and vegetables are highly susceptible to quality deterioration and spoilage resulting from ripening and senescence, respiratory metabolism, and microbial infection. These issues not only result in substantial economic losses but also increase the risk of foodborne illness. Although conventional packaging can provide basic physical protection against spoilage factors, it is limited by poor biodegradability, static efficacy, and inadequate tunability, which makes it incompatible with the multiple demands of green sustainability and high-quality preservation.
Scope and approach
To address these limitations and move beyond passive protection, smart packaging tailored to the postharvest physiological and pathological characteristics of fruits and vegetables offers innovative solutions for extending shelf life. Building upon a precise understanding of these characteristics, smart packaging techniques achieve precision preservation by regulating key factors that deteriorate, including atmospheric imbalance, ethylene-induced ripening, temperature or humidity fluctuations, and microbial proliferation. Meanwhile, artificial intelligence (AI) has further facilitated the development of smart packaging design and applications, serving as a powerful tool to accelerate the transformation from traditional trial-and-error design to predictive, in solico material development. This review systematically presents current research advances, highlighting the strategies for designing packaging according to fruit and vegetable characteristics and the AI implementation pathways. The review also comprehensively examined design frameworks, challenges, and potential resolutions for advancing packaging systems.
Key findings and conclusions
Smart packaging can achieve precision preservation aligned with the characteristics of produce, promoting the transformation of preservation packaging from passive protection to smart perception, dynamic regulation, and green regeneration. Furthermore, innovative approaches such as biomimetic materials, AI technology, supply chain monitoring, and biodegradability assessment can be incorporated to develop novel preservation packaging materials that better meet market requirements.

items.title: Unlocking the nutraceutical promise of edible flowers: An AI-driven approach to comprehensive chemical profiling
items.abstract:
Background
Edible flowers have long been valued across cultures for their vibrant appearance and culinary versatility. Recent studies have highlighted their rich nutrient and phytochemical profiles, positioning them as promising functional food ingredients.
Scope and approach
This review synthesizes literature from 2018 to 2025 on the nutritional, phytochemical, and health-promoting attributes of edible flowers. It presents analytical comparisons between conventional techniques (HPLC, GC-MS, NMR) and AI-enhanced methods (machine learning based pattern recognition, and spectral data mining) to evaluate their efficacy in compound identification and bioactivity prediction.
Key findings and conclusions
Major edible flowers contain high levels of flavonoids, polyphenols, anthocyanins, vitamins, and minerals, with compositional variability influenced by genotype, environment, and developmental stage. AI-based QSAR modeling and spectral data mining have improved the detection of low-abundance bioactive and supported mechanistic insights. Their applications span bakery products, beverages, and nutraceutical formulations, leveraging antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cardiovascular, neuroprotective, and anticancer properties. Culinary use at typical dosages shows minimal toxicity or allergenicity. Integrating omics technologies with AI data fusion is recommended to standardize phytochemical profiling, enhance model interpretability, and accelerate translation into validated functional foods and nutraceutical products.

items.title: AI-driven exploration of microbial resources in fermented foods
items.abstract:
Background
Fermented food microorganisms form a diverse microscopic ecosystem with significant potential for applications in food production, flavor development and human health. However, their complexity, the limitations of traditional culture methods, and the difficulty in functional analysis pose significant challenges to research. Together, these challenges restrict our understanding of underlying mechanisms.
Scope and approach
This review systematically outlines the paradigm shift brought by artificial intelligence (AI) in overcoming these limitations. We synthesize current research to detail the application of AI, particularly machine learning and deep learning, in mining and interpreting complex microbial datasets. Furthermore, we highlight the transformative applications and potential challenges of these computational methods in the fermentation food industry.
Key findings and conclusions
AI enables high-resolution microbial annotation and the accurate prediction of gene functions and novel metabolic pathways. Moreover, it empowers researchers to model the complex microbial interactions that drive food fermentation processes. Although challenges in data standardization, model interpretability, and real-world integration remain, AI has undoubtedly emerged as a transformative tool for mining microbial resources in fermented foods. It will accelerate the discovery of next-generation starter cultures and optimize fermentation processes for greater efficiency and consistency. These advancements are poised to significantly enhance industrial fermentation practices, supporting more sustainable and standardized food production. Furthermore, it will facilitate the creation of functional foods targeted at improving human health.
items.rationale: 综述 AI 挖掘发酵食品微生物基因功能、代谢通路与群落相互作用。

items.title: AI-driven precision protease engineering for the food industry
items.abstract: Advances inst traditional protease hurdles, a new frontier in protease engineering, include the high-efficiency design of tailored variants. A central challenge in modern enzyme engineering is designing highly efficient proteases tailored to specific industrial applications. Artificial intelligence (AI) is now providing powerful solutions to these problems. By integrating established strategies, such as directed evolution and rational design, the capacity of AI to analyze enzyme structures and predict mutational outcomes has substantially enhanced the stability and adaptability of proteases. This synergy extends beyond mere optimization to enable the de novo design of novel proteases. This review provides an overview of the importance of this capability in the food industry as AI-driven design paves the way for safer and more sustainable production methods to meet the demands of precision food production. These innovations collectively represent an important advance toward enhancing the performance and enabling the sustainable production of industrial proteases. The next frontier may involve the deep integration of AI with multi-omics data, a necessary step to expand protease applications and improve the nutritional quality of biotechnology food products. The integration of multi-omics with AI-guided de novo design has expanded protease applications in food biotechnology, addressing the evolving demands of industrial processes while enhancing food quality and nutritional value.
items.rationale: 综述 AI 结构预测、突变设计与多组学用于食品工业蛋白酶工程。

items.title: AI-driven food bioprocessing: How far its integration with practice?
items.abstract:
Background
Bioprocessing strengthens modern food manufacturing, yet faces growing challenges related to efficiency, scalability, and sustainability under increasing global food demand. Traditional fermentation and enzymatic processes remain highly empirical, leading to fluctuating outcomes and resource inefficiency. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning offer opportunities to enhance precision, optimize processes, and accelerate the transition toward intelligent and sustainable food biomanufacturing systems.
Scope and approach
We provide an integrated overview of how AI is revolutionizing food bioprocessing across multiple domains. We critically review recent progress in food bioprocessing, including enzyme engineering, metabolic engineering, and the construction of synthetic microbial consortia by AI-driven modelling and learning algorithms. Furthermore, we highlight advances in process optimization through real-time monitoring, consistency assessment and predictive analytics. Emerging applications of AI in contamination detection and food traceability systems are also examined. Finally, we discuss the advancements and limitations of this rapidly evolving field, while envisioning future directions toward truly intelligent food bioprocessing systems.
Key findings and conclusion
AI shows substantial potential to enhance process predictability, productivity, and resource efficiency in food bioprocessing, especially in enzyme design, process optimization, and real-time quality assurance. However, the industrial implementation remains constrained by data quality, model interpretability, and safety accountability. Future research should focus on developing bioprocessing-specific AI frameworks that embed domain knowledge, regulatory requirements, and food safety constraints into core design principles, moving beyond isolated algorithmic improvements toward coordinated system-level innovation to support productivity, safety, sustainability, and societal trust as required by the evolving demands of future food industries.
items.rationale: 综述 AI 对食品发酵、酶与代谢工程、工艺优化和质量监控的应用。

items.title: Transforming from ‘natural tools’ into ‘custom sensors’: combining directionally designed biological nanopore electrochemistry sensing lumens with AI-driven analytics to pioneer a new paradigm for food analysis
items.abstract:
Background
The detection of trace level analytes in complex food matrices faces dual challenges: identifying hazards threatening public safety and characterizing beneficial micronutrients. Achieving both high sensitivity and excellent specificity in detection represents a critical requirement for advancing food safety and quality control. Inspired by biological molecular recognition and transmembrane transport, biological nanopores have emerged as promising sensing elements capable of capturing and identifying single target molecules.
Scope and approach
This review first provides an overview of construction and working principles of biological nanopore based single-molecule sensing platforms, detailing key design strategies and engineering approaches. Furthermore, this review aims to highlight cutting-edge developments and trends in AI-enhanced nanopore electrochemistry sensing, including deep learning-assisted signal analysis, dynamic simulation-guided design, and de novo design novel channel proteins, emphasizing the necessity of interdisciplinary integration. Subsequently, we comprehensively reviewed recent frontier applications of biological nanopore in food analysis.
Key findings and conclusions
Biological nanopore technology offers significant advantages for food analysis, including label-free, high-throughput, and low-cost operation while providing unique single-molecule resolution and rich physicochemical information. From data analysis to sensor design, the participation of artificial intelligence is decisively advancing this field. These developments anticipate the wider practical application of nanopore sensing in enhancing both food safety monitoring and nutritional quality assessment in the future.

items.title: AI-driven design of next-generation food starter cultures: from empirical screening to intelligent customization
items.abstract:
Background
Food starter cultures are central to shaping flavor, texture, and nutritional functionality in fermented foods. However, current food starter culture development faces several key challenges, including low screening efficiency, unclear function and limited understanding of microbial interactions. In addition, the growing demand for high-quality fermented foods and improved food safety requires the development of well-defined, reliable and functional tailored food starter cultures.
Scope and approach
This review systematically examines the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with multi-omics technologies in starter culture research. We summarize the evolution of starter culture development, and critically analyze recent advances in AI-driven approaches for decoding microbial interactions, predicting metabolic functions, and optimizing fermentation processes.
Key findings and conclusions
Food starter culture development is undergoing a paradigm shift from empirical screening to data-driven and function-oriented design. AI-enabled models, particularly machine learning and deep learning, facilitate the integration of multi-omics datasets to unravel complex microbial interaction networks and predict flavor-related metabolic pathways with high accuracy. Emerging frameworks such as genome-scale metabolic models, cascade reaction and digital twins further enable the rational design and optimization of fermentation systems from a systems biology perspective.
Despite these advances, major challenges remain, including limited data standardization, insufficient model interpretability, and barriers to industrial translation. Addressing these issues will be critical for bridging the gap between computational prediction and real-world application.
Overall, AI is poised to become a key enabling technology for the next generation of starter cultures, supporting the transition toward precision fermentation and customized food design.
items.rationale: 综述 AI 与多组学预测发酵菌种功能、微生物互作与代谢过程。

items.title: Beyond high accuracy: a cross-technology framework for validating AI driven mycotoxin screening in complex food matrices
items.abstract:
Background
Recent literature frequently couples optical sensing with machine learning for mycotoxin screening, often reporting accuracies exceeding 95%. However, industrial adoption appears limited. We hypothesize this translational gap likely stems from a systemic disconnect between laboratory-generated computational accuracy and the physical robustness required in field environments.
Scope and approach
Unlike previous reviews cataloging algorithmic advancements, this study takes a fundamentally different, problem-driven approach. Synthesizing primary literature (2020–2026), we found that exceptional performances can sometimes be influenced by methodological artifacts: conflating fungal biomass with direct toxin detection, bypassing natural infections via artificial spiking, and using internal validation susceptible to spatial data leakage. To systematically re-evaluate published models against deployment criteria, the evidence robustness framework (ERF) was introduced, assessing sample authenticity, validation rigor, matrix dynamics, regulatory alignment, and model transparency.
Key findings and conclusions
To enhance comparability and regulatory legibility, the minimum information for AI modeling (MI-AIM) reporting checklist is proposed. Transitioning from laboratory to industrial deployment will likely require broader methodological shifts rather than isolated algorithmic enhancements. By outlining actionable pathways, including multimodal digital twins and physics-informed explainable AI, this review aims to guide a cultural shift toward transparent reporting of external-validation metrics, helping establish these platforms as trusted, industry-ready food-safety tools.
items.rationale: 综述 AI 霉菌毒素筛查模型的外部验证、矩阵效应和食品安全适用性。

items.title: Toward closing the loop: safe autonomy, validation, and trust in AI-driven nonthermal food processing
items.abstract:
Background
Nonthermal food processing can preserve product quality while reducing microbial hazards, but treatment efficacy varies with the food matrix, microorganism, and equipment. Artificial intelligence (AI) can support prediction and process adjustment. However, accurate models and automated equipment do not by themselves establish safe autonomous processing.
Scope and approach
This critical review examines AI-assisted nonthermal food processing through a Level 0–5 framework that distinguishes conventional processing, offline modeling, soft sensing, real-time monitoring, bounded intervention, and safety-constrained closed-loop control. It evaluates cold plasma, pulsed light and ultraviolet-C, pulsed electric fields, high-pressure processing, ultrasound, and ionizing radiation. The assessment connects reported measurements and model functions with physical actuation, response time, microbiological validation, and regulatory requirements, while distinguishing primary experimental findings from proposals and secondary sources.
Key findings and conclusions
Most reported applications support offline prediction, optimization, or product-state estimation. Two primary studies implement physical feedback that regulates circulation flow or generator duty cycle, but neither adjusts treatment using a validated microbial-safety state. The reviewed evidence does not establish bounded intervention or constrained closed-loop microbial-safety control in nonthermal processing. Sensor availability, rapid computation, and favorable predictive accuracy are therefore insufficient measures of control readiness. Progress requires validated relationships between measurable signals and microbial response, resistant-strain and matrix-specific challenge testing, uncertainty assessment near safety limits, and measured end-to-end latency. Previously validated operating limits, defined change-control procedures, cybersecurity, and human oversight provide a practical basis for testing higher autonomy without weakening established food-safety requirements.

items.title: LGINet: Linguistic guided image diffusion model for tree species generation and identification from aerial imagery
items.abstract: A key challenge in applying AI to forest monitoring is tree species identification, hindered by complex visual variations and limited data of tree canopies. Moreover, AI-assisted recognition frameworks that effectively integrate large language models with human knowledge bases in forestry have not yet been fully established. Against this background, this study introduces linguistic guided image diffusion model (LGINet), a framework integrating textually guided image generation with tree species detection to enhance forest applications through technological synergy. The framework comprises three key methodological components: (1) A module designed to leverage detailed textual descriptions specific to forest environments, incorporating elements such as species traits, spatial layout, and phenological features. It generates text embeddings that are semantically aligned with forest knowledge. (2) An innovative diffusion-based framework integrates an improved U-Net architecture with Markov chain theory and textual semantic embeddings, fusing noisy images with forest-specific linguistic semantics to generate highly realistic aerial tree images. (3) An optimized detection pipeline utilizing the generated images, based on an enhanced YOLOv11 architecture with a context-aware feature extractor and adaptive anchor scaling, enabling efficient, large-scale tree crown detection and species identification. Experimental evaluations validate the efficacy of the proposed framework, with the image generation module achieving a Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) of 0.94 and a Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) score of 6.42, demonstrating exceptional fidelity in synthetic output quality. Furthermore, the detection pipeline attained a mean Average Precision (mAP50) of 0.868 in species identification tasks, consistently outperforming all baseline models across evaluation metrics. The integrated system improves capabilities of forest species detection by leveraging linguistic-driven synthesis to generate high-fidelity forest imagery and tree species identification.

items.title: Bridging the gap between computer vision and bioelectrical signal analysis
items.abstract: Bioelectrical signals are vital for non-invasive physiological monitoring and disease diagnosis. The application of artificial intelligence (AI) in automatic bioelectrical signal analysis has garnered attention. However, training supervised AI models requires abundant labeled data, which is particularly challenging in medical scenarios. Existing transfer learning (TL) approaches attempt to transfer knowledge from images in the computer vision (CV) domain, but face significant challenges due to dimensional difference and distribution gaps between CV and bioelectrical signal domains. Traditional domain adaptation (DA) assumes domain task invariance and focuses mainly on feature distribution difference, without considering label inconsistency and the complex cross-dimensional scenarios. Our motivation is to address the fundamental challenges in cross-domain knowledge transfer by jointly solving the dimensional gap and task discrepancy between CV and bioelectrical signal domains, thereby facilitating robust learning with limited labeled medical data. In this paper, we propose a cross-dimensional information transfer (CDIT) framework that enables effective information fusion through parallel encoding-decoding modules, which preserve the discriminative characteristics of both two-dimensional (2D) CV images and one-dimensional (1D) bioelectrical signals while mapping them into a shared feature space. Furthermore, we develop a cross-task DA method that synergistically integrates feature and label information to address the label inconsistency challenge in the DA phase of CDITF. We conduct extensive experiments on two representative scenarios using six databases. The experimental results demonstrate that CDITF with cross-task DA (CDITF-CTDA) achieves successful knowledge transfer from CV into bioelectrical signal domains despite their inherent difference, consistently outperforming baseline methods with improvements of 0.02–0.07 in AUC for bioelectrical signal analysis. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of CDITF-CTDA in leveraging CV knowledge for bioelectrical signal analysis under limited-labeled data medical scenarios.

items.title: GDCF-Net: A generative-discriminative contrastive fusion network for multi-class fault diagnosis of power transformer
items.abstract:
High-voltage power systems depend on main transformers whose unexpected faults can cascade into costly outages and safety risks. Condition monitoring in practice must operate under shifting operating regimes, heterogeneous equipment and sensors across substations, aging media, and pervasive measurement noise—conditions that induce domain shift, scarce and imbalanced labels, and fragile feature separability. Rule-based diagnosis remains valuable for transparency yet maintaining accuracy and cross-machine reliability under these constraints is challenging. We propose Generative-Discriminative Contrastive Fusion Network (GDCF-Net), a multi-level fusion framework built around three complementary layers that operate in concert. (1) Representation fusion: a conditional variational alignment matches the training posterior 𝑞⁡(𝑧|𝑥,𝑦)
 to the test-time prior 𝑝⁡(𝑧|𝑥)
 via a KL regularization, closing the train–inference gap and avoiding label leakage; a supervised contrastive objective shapes both posterior and prior latent means to tighten intra-class cohesion and enlarge inter-class margins. (2) Feature fusion: a cross-attention classifier uses the latent as Query and the original feature projections as Key and Value, fusing latent semantics back into the raw feature space to surface class-salient cues and support interpretability. (3) Decision fusion: a lightweight prototype head with EMA-updated prototypes and prior-adjustment logit to produce energy scores for imbalance calibration and open-set rejection, which are fused with the classifier logits. The network is trained end to end with a compact joint loss that combines reconstruction, KL divergence, supervised contrast, and classification, with optional prototype regularization.; inference uses the prior path only, and the decoder is train-only, keeping latency low. Across two real-world datasets, GDCF-Net consistently outperforms representative ML/DL baselines and a rule-based benchmark in weighted F1 under class imbalance and domain shift. Ablation experiments, where the representation-, feature-, and decision-level fusion modules are incrementally introduced, demonstrate progressive gains in classification performance. Furthermore, unknown-fault experiments confirm that the proposed fusion design maintains robustness in realistic industrial conditions; measured FLOPs indicate suitability for deployment. GDCF-Net advances accurate, interpretable, and deployable transformer fault diagnosis under real-world imbalance and domain shift, supporting reliable cross-machine monitoring in modern power systems.

items.title: MoMD Transformer: adaptive multi-modal fault diagnosis via knowledge transfer with vibration-current signals
items.abstract: Fault diagnosis is crucial to ensure the reliable and safe operation of electromechanical systems in the manufacturing industry. Recently, multi-modal data fusion based fault diagnosis methods have achieved remarkable progress. However, these methods impose additional constraints on industrial scenarios because they require the simultaneous input of multi-modal data during the inference phase, which limits their applicability in cases where only single-modal data acquisition is feasible during operation. To overcome this limitation, a novel Mixture-of-Modality-Diagnosis (MoMD) Transformer is proposed in this paper for adaptive multi-modal fault diagnosis with vibration and current signals. In this model, we improve the feed-forward network in Transformer into a multi-channel structure to adaptively process multiple modalities. Additionally, to address the challenge of weak fault signatures in current modality, we design a global knowledge transfer module that utilizes vibration features to guide the feature learning for current signals. Specifically, our comprehensive analysis of feature alignment strategies reveals that the one-to-one paradigm is superior to contrastive learning paradigm for fault data, given its low intra-class variance. Moreover, to enhance the representation ability for time-series signals, the masked signal modeling task is introduced into the training phase, thereby improving the diagnostic accuracy. Experimental results on two datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior diagnostic accuracy, reaching 99.96 % and 100 % respectively, outperforming other methods in various modality-availability scenarios.

items.title: Beyond single prototype: A multi-prototype fusion framework with contrastive learning and diffusion model for zero-shot fault diagnosis
items.abstract: Compound faults are becoming more frequent in rotating machinery due to the increasing complexity of industrial equipment. However, acquiring fault data, particularly compound fault data, remains challenging. Recent progress in zero-shot learning has provided techniques capable of recognizing unseen compound faults even when no corresponding samples are available during training. Nevertheless, existing approaches are limited due to domain shift and feature confusion problems, which compromise diagnostic accuracy. To address these problems, a triple-prototype fusion (TPF) framework is developed for zero-shot fault diagnosis. First, a prototype fusion framework is constructed to address the domain shift issue. This framework fuses the generated prototype of the simulated faults, the feature prototype derived from the actual faults, and the theoretical prototype constructed by the prior knowledge, thereby alleviating the problem of domain shift caused by insufficient information from the single prototype. Then, a multi-distribution fusion contrastive learning mechanism is developed to solve the feature fusion problem. This mechanism introduces the multivariate prior information of distributions when generating positive samples, making the constructed positive sample more discriminative. Additionally, a model-sample stabilization diffusion model is proposed to enhance the stability of sample generation. The model introduces stability mechanisms from model training and sample denoising perspectives to comprehensively improve the stability of generated samples. The effectiveness of the TPF framework is verified through two experimental cases. The TPF framework enables the diagnosis of unseen compound faults without requiring any compound fault data for training. Benchmarking against eight typical models and advanced zero-shot learning methods, the TPF achieves favorable performance. The code will be available at https://github.com/QinYi-team/TPF.

items.title: DAP-former: A physics-aware dual-stream fusion transformer for robust industrial time-series forecasting
items.abstract: Precise time series forecasting in complex industrial systems (e.g., power grids and environmental monitoring) essentially requires the effective fusion of signal energy and structural timing information. However, existing methods often suffer from amplitude-phase entanglement, where high-frequency noise disrupts the learning of intrinsic topological structures, leading to the prevalent phase lag problem. To address this, we propose DAP-Former (A Physics-Aware Dual-Stream Fusion Transformer), a robust frequency-domain framework that establishes a novel Decouple-then-Fuse paradigm. Unlike traditional architectures that process entangled features, DAP-Former introduces a Dual-Stream Fusion Architecture: (1) An Amplitude Stream that captures global energy dependencies; and (2) A Phase Stream that employs a physics-aware indirect estimation mechanism to recover structural timing from noisy spectra robustly. These two orthogonal information flows are then synthesized via a Holo-Fusion mechanism to reconstruct time-domain signals with high fidelity. Extensive evaluations on 17 benchmarks show DAP-Former achieves SOTA in 85% of cases, notably reducing long-horizon MSE by 14.8% (0.363) on ETTh1. Under severe 50% noise, it restricts degradation to +15.5% compared to  > +60% for entangled models, while improving industrial emission tracking by 38.7%. Finally, it ensures 33% faster convergence and a 14.1 ms inference latency, offering a robust and lightweight solution for real-time industrial edge deployment.

items.title: Conditional diffusion transformer enabled few-shot spatiotemporal modeling
items.abstract: Transformer-based models excel at spatiotemporal modeling but degrade in few-shot settings due to limited data and attention noise, which hampers meaningful representation learning. To overcome this, we propose Conditional Diffusion Transformer (CDT), which integrates generative pretraining via diffusion modeling with task-specific fine-tuning. CDT learns to reconstruct spatiotemporal structures from noise using a graph-based diffusion module with hierarchical pooling and upsampling, capturing both global spatial dependencies and local temporal dynamics. During fine-tuning, the diffusion module generates auxiliary structural features conditioned on downstream task data. These features are adaptively fused with task-specific representations via a cross-attention transformer, enhancing robustness and generalization in sparse-data scenarios. By combining generative priors with attention-based modeling, CDT achieves superior few-shot spatiotemporal forecasting performance. Experiments on three real-world datasets show that CDT outperforms state-of-the-art attention- and linear-based baselines under limited data regimes. Additionally, the pre-training conditional diffusion process on a large dataset demonstrates the ability to learn inherent features. These results highlight the potential of diffusion-based pretraining for enhancing spatiotemporal modeling in few-shot scenarios. Codes can be found at https://github.com/CodingMaker2/CDT.

items.title: TENG-based self-powered knee joint motion decoding and AI-assisted evaluation system
items.abstract: The growing prevalence of knee degenerative diseases has increased the demand for lightweight, continuous, and quantitative monitoring technologies for home-based functional assessment. Herein, a sliding freestanding-layer knee-motion triboelectric nanogenerator (KM-TENG) is developed for self-powered knee motion decoding and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted functional evaluation. A 3D-printed elastic traction structure converts rotational knee motion into controllable linear sliding. By integrating a biomass composite triboelectric layer and interdigital-block coupled electrodes, the KM-TENG achieves stable electrical output and displacement encoding. Cyclic tests verify excellent long-term stability, and continuous knee angle decoding is achieved with an angular resolution of approximately 4.77°. After optical flow calibration and time delay correction, the decoded angular trajectories show high consistency with references. Combined with mechanical modeling and commercial force gauge calibration, leave-one-subject-out cross-validation yields a mean absolute error of 3.56 N and a mean percentage error of only 0.96%. Based on multi-dimensional kinematic, mechanical, and triboelectric features, the AI-assisted module realizes interpretable feedback for motion quality evaluation, load risk warning, and rehabilitation guidance. This passive, lightweight, and low-cost wearable scheme provides reliable technical support for early screening of knee degeneration and home-based rehabilitation assessment.

items.title: AI-enabled flexible sensing technologies for safety engineering: Materials, devices, and applications
items.abstract: Safety engineering underpins the resilience and stability of modern industrial and societal infrastructures; however, conventional rigid monitoring systems remain constrained by limited conformability, adaptability and real-time responsiveness in complex and dynamic environments. The convergence of flexible electronics and artificial intelligence (AI) offers a transformative route from passive signal acquisition to active cognitive decision-making. Here, we provide a systematic overview of AI-enabled flexible sensing systems for critical safety applications. We first categorize functional materials by dimensionality and discuss material design strategies that enable mechanical compliance, environmental robustness and sensing capability. Building upon this materials foundation, we further examine computational architectures that transform multimodal sensing signals into actionable intelligence, with emphasis on deep learning-based diagnostics, edge computing frameworks, and neuromorphic devices that alleviate centralized processing constraints. We contextualize these advances across representative safety scenarios, including structural health monitoring, occupational risk assessment, power infrastructure inspection, and fire detection. Finally, we discuss the key challenges, including reliability, scalability, and long-term stability, that must be addressed to enable the transition from assisted monitoring toward autonomous and resilient safety systems. By bridging materials innovation and intelligent computation, AI-enabled flexible sensing technologies are positioned to shift safety engineering from reactive protection to predictive and cognitive paradigms.
